findings.claim: No test checks that TextPreview still marks and scrolls to a `highlight` term after the text loads. The only highlight test checks that nothing scrolls while loading.
findings.impact: A later change could stop search-term highlighting in every text viewer and the suite would stay green. Two examples: dropping the `useHighlightPassage` call from TextLines, or passing `ready=false`. The upcoming plain-text Read view (I6) will reuse TextLines and relies on this behaviour.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/__tests__/TextPreview.test.tsx:42-57 is the only test that passes `highlight`. It asserts `scrollIntoView` is not called while fetch never resolves. A grep of that file for `highlight|scrollIntoView` finds nothing else. TextLines.tsx:86 `useHighlightPassage(preRef, highlight, true)` is the only thing that applies the mark.
findings.repro: Mutation (by reading): delete `useHighlightPassage(preRef, highlight, true);` in TextLines.tsx. The new test still passes because nothing scrolls, and the other tests pass no highlight. So no test fails.

bucket_proposal.reason: No code defect. This is a coverage gap: one-sided assertions in the fix's own test leave the positive case of the guarded behaviour unpinned. I8's list for TextPreview does not include highlight.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a test that resolves fetch with text containing the term and asserts a `mark.ask-citation-highlight` appears and `scrollIntoView` is called once.

findings.claim: The highlight hook's `scrolledRef` now lives in TextLines, which unmounts during every load. If TextPreview's `fileId` changes while `highlight` stays the same, the page now scrolls to the term again. Before the extraction it did not, because the ref survived in TextPreview and was reset only when the quote changed.
findings.impact: Only reachable if FilePreview reuses one TextPreview instance across files with the same highlight. FilePreview.tsx:236 renders TextPreview with no key, so it depends on whether the parent remounts per file. The result would be an extra scroll to the mark on the new file, which is arguably the more correct behaviour. Nothing silently breaks.
findings.evidence: useHighlightPassage.ts:65-69 keeps `scrolledRef` per hook instance and resets it only on a change of `quote`. TextPreview.tsx:152-158 returns the loading block whenever `loading || content === null`, which unmounts TextLines (TextLines.tsx:83-86) on each fetch. FilePreview.tsx:236-242 renders `<TextPreview fileId={file.id} …>` with no key.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (by reading only; I did not trace whether FilePreview's parent remounts per file)

bucket_proposal.reason: Scroll timing across file changes is not covered by any declared invariant. This is a small behaviour difference in a refactor declared behaviour-preserving.

specification_compliance: Fix 9de832c87 resolves r1 F2. TextPreview.tsx:152 returns the loading block while `content === null`, so TextLines (and its hook, which has `ready=true`) mounts only with loaded text. No early scrollIntoView runs on an empty <pre>.

Moving the error branch ahead of the loading branch does not change behaviour. The effect sets `loading=true` and `error=null` together (TextPreview.tsx:104-105), and failure sets the error then `loading=false` in the same batch, so the two states are never both shown.
The new test kills the r1 behaviour. Under the r1 code the first render mounted TextLines with "", and the effect called `container.scrollIntoView` synchronously within render's act().
The TextLines extraction keeps decorate(), its limits, bare-CR folding and both rendering branches unchanged (I8 for TextPreview). The `MAX_DECORATED_LINES` re-export is preserved.
r1 F3 (capture controller not published during the prompt, loading or error states) is unchanged by the fixes. Behaviour is the same as at r1.
Commits 8040bfe87 and 88e897df4 are review records only. No protected path is edited.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The highlight scroll state now resets each time TextLines remounts, that is, on every load including a fileId change with the same highlight (F2).
regression_risks: The future plain-text Read view (I6) requires a single scroll per open. TextLines' hook resets per mount, so remounting Read on each switch to Read would scroll again unless the scroll state is lifted above TextLines.
The capture controller is still null outside the loaded state (r1 F3, still open).
test_coverage: New test TextPreview.test.tsx:42-57 pins 'no scroll while loading' and fails against the r1 code.
No positive highlight test exists (mark applied, scroll after load). See F1.
No test covers the over-1 MB Load prompt followed by a highlight, and no direct TextLines test exists.
not_verified: I could not run the test suite or the build. Whether the new test passes under jsdom (Element.prototype.scrollIntoView stubbing) was reasoned, not run.
Whether FilePreview's parents remount TextPreview per file (this bears on F2).
Whether the knowledge addon's capture action reacts to the null controller during loading (r1 F3).
trajectory: One code fix round so far: 9de832c87. It merges `content === null` into the existing loading branch and moves the error branch ahead of it. This adds no new state, prop or prediction. It widens one existing guard so TextLines only mounts with loaded text, and it removes the `content ?? \"\"` fallback, so a code path was removed rather than added. No earlier fix round exists for it to repeat, and nothing so far suggests the design is being patched. The other two commits (8040bfe87, 88e897df4) only record reviews.
